w: One of the most colorful events of the festival was the grand procession of dieties, that took place on the eve of the Mandir consecration ceremony. The procession was flagged off from Uhuru Park, in Nairobi’s City Center, at exactly 2.50 p.m. Nine beautifully designed floats were created, which carried the idols to be installed in the temple. Never before had the Nairobians seen something as colorful and joyous as this. The procession proceeded through Kenyatta Avenue, Moi Avenue, down the Slip Road leading to Globe Roundabout, Muranga Road, Limuru Road, and finally turned to Forest Road to enter the new Mandir. Throughout the procession the weather remained dry and cool, which proved to be a blessing for participants. Over 4,000 people participated in the Nagar Yatra, which covered a distance of well over 10 kms. Estimates indicate that close to 15,000 Nairobians had lined up along the streets to witness the 1.5 kms long procession. The famous Yogi Marching Band was at the forefront of the procession, leading the rest of the masses through Nairobi’s streets. Shree Aksharpurushottam Maharaj’s boat-like float was the first among the floats and it also had a troupe of saints singing devotional songs to the accompaniment of musical instruments. This float was followed by the elegantly designed floats of Shree Bhagatji Maharaj, Shree Shastriji Maharaj, Shree Yogiji Maharaj, Shree Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Shree Laxmi Narayan Dev, Shree Radha Krishna Dev and finally the float which carried Shree Hanumanji and Shree Ganapatiji. Amongst the participants there were saints, devotees from various centres as well as prominent members of Nairobi’s Hindu Community. Hundreds of youths, teenagers and children adorned in traditional Indian costumes added spice to the grand event. All major newspapers and TV channels covered the spectacular mega - procession.At 4.55 p.m.the procession finally concluded at the New Mandir where HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed everyone with words of wisdom.

Kanubhai Amin, a devotee, brought his mentally retarded son, Samir, to be blessed by Swamishri. Then he expressed his anxiety, "Swami, my son does not even know who's puja he does and who is Swaminarayan. How will he be redeemed?" "It will be done. Since he was born in your home, he will be redeemed," Swamishri assured. Then Kanubhai expressed his frustration, "This son of mine is like Jad Bharat." "That's good. You can worship God without any hassle," Swamishri replied. "But what will happen to him when my wife and I die?" Kanubhai asked. "You should not think of that. God is looking after him now and will care for him afterwards. It is He who looks after everyone." Swamishri reassured the devotee that God is the sustainer of all life.
If one remains humble then he will be honored with praises. And if one remains arrogant then people will not love him.
By remaining humble one accomplishes one's work easily.

At 10.00 a.m. In the presence of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, Swamishri told sadhus to chant Vedic mantras while he worshipped the Narmada waters by showering sanctified flowers. When Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami split a coconut and sprinkled its water into the Narmada canal Swamishri responded, "Jai Maharaj. May the waters flow forever and may it reach Saurashtra and Kutch ..."
At 7.00 p.m. The pujan rituals were carried out in a boat amidst Vedic chantings, worship of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and arti by Swamishri and the Chief Minister. ( See special News report )

In the evening assembly, youths performed a wonderful traditional dance on the lyric, "Swaminarayan charan kamalma..." Thereafter Swamishri was honored with garlands, flower shawls and gifts by sadhus and youths. Inspiring incidents of youths in Vadodara Satsang Mandal were then narrated in the assembly. A debate on, "Is Study or Character Greater?" was effectively presented by youths.

Finally, Swamishri blessed the Youth Day assembly, "Character is more important because it endows you with humility, discrimination, the virtue to serve others, to not get angry, to tolerate and to do good. Whereas one who has advanced academically will not be able to tolerate. He will become agitated and angry. We cannot discount studies, however character is the greater of the two ornaments... To run our lives financially and to run our world through the technology we have invented, we need academic studies. But the glory and importance of that lies in having character. It is character that decorates our mundane works..."

Day 2 - National Bal-Balika Shibir 2004 The balaks sang kirtans, recited mukhpath and performed a dance in Swamishri's puja. Swamishri also launched the 'Pramukh Cup', a 7-a-side football tournament, and also pleased a young balak by enticing him to grab the football whilst he continuously moved it in his hands. This little action brought a smile to everyone in the audience. The morning session of the shibir saw senior sadhus speaking on the importance of remembering divine moments with Swamishri on a regular basis.

The balaks then went to play the Pramukh Cup Tournament held at Alperton Goals. From throughout the UK, 42 teams participated in the tournament, which was won by Saturday London Mandir Bal Mandal Team A. In the evening session, Swamishri presented the trophy to the winning team.

Day 2 - National Family Shibir 2004 During the day there were a series of talks and panel discussions on understanding Swamishri's wishes. Yuvaks took niyams to do puja daily, tilak- chandlo regularly and to attend the weekly assembly on time. The final session of the shibir was on the topic of faith in God. Swamishri stressed in his blessings the importance of steadfastly abiding by the principles of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The finale of this shibir was the Fuldol celebration, in which all the yuvaks and balaks were sprayed by Swamishri with the saffron-coloured water sanctified by Shri Harikrishna Maharaj.

The day commenced with balaks singing a prarthana in the Mandir while Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed darshan. The balaks then performed kirtans, recited mukhpath and performed a dance in Swamishri’s puja. Swamishri also launched the ‘Pramukh Cup’ 7-a -side football tournament and also pleased a young balak by enticing him to grab the football whilst he continuously moved his hands. This little action brought a smile to everyone in the audience.
The morning session of the Shibir saw senior sadhus speaking on the importance of remembering divine moments with Swamishri on a regular basis.

The balaks then went to play the Pramukh Cup Tournament held at Alperton Goals. 42 teams participated in the tournament which was won by Saturday London Mandir Bal Mandal Team A. In the evening session, Swamishri presented the trophy to the winning team.

Trustees of The Heritage Trust, based in Surat, came for Swamishri’s darshan. They had published a book entitled Sanskruti Purush Pramukh Swami, which had been written for them by Vivekpriya Swami. Mahant Swami performed the inauguration of the book.
Today, after a heartfelt farewell from Atladra, as Mahant Swami Maharaj set out for Anand, he asked for his mala.
Seeing this, the attendants asked, "Once, when you were coming from Delhi to Ahmedabad with Swamibapa, Swamibapa turned his mala continuously throughout the journey. What were you doing then?"
"I was having darshan of Swamibapa."
The guru, by continuously turning his mala, sets the ideal of supreme devotion, and the disciple, by continuously having darshan of the guru, sets the ideal of devotion to the guru! What a rare pair!
During the journey the sadhus asked another question: "Did you have darshan of Shastriji Maharaj?"
"When I was six months old, Ashabhai took me to Shastriji Maharaj. Shastriji Maharaj gave me vartman (initiation). Then when Shastriji Maharaj passed away to Akshardham, I went."

Today, at the tribute assembly for Swamibapa held at Anand, giving his blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "In the life of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the line 'Call him a true Vaishnav who feels the pain of others' was embodied. He had countless virtues such as boundless patience, humility and forgiveness. The work he did, no one can do. The works he did are to be carried forward with everyone's cooperation."
Thus waves of devotion to his guru kept surging in Swamishri's words.
